FUTURES UNITS, MEASURED 2026-09-16 from this board's own refusal in data/index.json, not from a fixture and not from the arithmetic: every one of the 6 testable row(s) on this board fails cash - basis = futures when the futures column is read as cents, and every one balances when it is read as DOLLARS. On the rows the refusal printed: cash 5.02 basis -0.32 needs 534c, the column reads 5.3375 which is -528.663c as cents and -0.25c as dollars; cash 5.13 basis -0.21 needs 534c, the column reads 5.3375 which is -528.663c as cents and -0.25c as dollars. The two hypotheses are a hundred apart, which is three orders of magnitude past anything a bid board can produce, so this is read off the board rather than fitted to it. Declared, not inferred, and self-checking: a wrong declaration is out by a hundredfold and the identity guard refuses it straight back.

CASH ROUNDING, MEASURED 2026-09-16 across 47 rows on the 25 cashbidssingle boards refused for this same reason: under the dollars hypothesis the residuals are -0.25c (17), +0c (2), +0.25c (24), +0.5c (4) and nothing else. Worst is 0.5c, they run in BOTH directions, and they sit on the quarter-cent grid — the board posts cash and basis to two decimals and its quote on the quarter cent, so the derived value is a whole number of cents and the quote is not. floor-cent does not describe this: it explains only the non-negative ones. round-cent-both bounds it at strictly under a cent either way, which is exactly what two cent-rounded columns can produce between them, and it still refuses every column shift, which moves things by tens of cents.
